frontmatter.raw:
name: taste-design-review
description: |
  Structured visual and usability audit of existing interfaces — landing pages, SaaS apps, portfolios. Screenshot-first review against taste rules, Nielsen heuristics, and accessibility floor; severity-ranked findings with specific fixes; before/after verification. Use when asked to critique, review, or improve an existing UI.
triggers:
  - "design review"
  - "visual audit"
  - "ux critique"
  - "review my site"
  - "make this page better"
  - "design feedback"

triggers.text: Structured visual and usability audit of existing interfaces — landing pages, SaaS apps, portfolios. evidence.text: Structured visual and usability audit of existing interfaces — landing pages, SaaS apps, portfolios. Screenshot-first review against taste rules, Nielsen heuristics, and accessibility floor; severity-ranked findings with specific fixes; before/after verification. Use when asked to critique, review, or improve an existing UI.

items.text: **Capture:** full-page screenshots of every viewport (desktop 1440, tablet 768, mobile 390). Review what is, not what you think is.
**First read (8 seconds):** what does this page say it is? Can you name the product, audience, and primary action without scrolling?
**Structured pass:** apply the checks below, in order.
**Rank findings:** P0 (broken/legal/blocking) / P1 (seriously undermines quality) / P2 (polish) / P3 (preference).
**Fix in ranked order** with atomic changes; re-screenshot and verify each fix didn't break the design argument.
**Report:** findings table with screenshot references, severity, and the one-sentence fix for each.

**The kill question:** could this page have been generated by a default agent (slop patterns: purple gradients, centered hero + 3 cards, emoji icons, Inter-only, rounded-2xl, browser-chrome screenshot)? Every "yes" is a P1.
**Hierarchy:** one dominant element per viewport; does the eye land where the business wants it?
**Type:** any text under 10px, more than 3 weights, no display contrast, body full-width, 6-line paragraphs, widows in headings.
**Color:** more than ~3 meaningful colors, gradients doing decoration, accent used >4 times per viewport, white text on pale fills, contrast failures (exact: 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large / 3:1 UI).
**Alignment:** elements sharing an edge line up (check visually); hairline grid vs. floating cards scattered; spacing scale integrity (any 7px or 13px paddings?).
**Depth:** shadows as the only depth source; glass everywhere; cards inside cards inside cards.
**Visibility of system status** (2–3s): every action produces feedback; no dead buttons; loading states exist.
**Match with the real world:** language is the user's, not the company's ("deploy instance" on a consumer site = fail).
**User control & freedom:** exit routes everywhere; undo exists for destructive acts.
**Consistency:** same action looks the same everywhere; one style of button; one way to reach the same destination.
**Error prevention:** destructive actions confirmed; submit buttons guarded; autocomplete on forms.
**Recognition over recall:** no invented jargon; navigation names are self-explanatory.
**Flexibility:** shortcuts for repeat users (search, keyboard) without cluttering the novice path.
**Aesthetic & minimalist:** anything that hides the primary action is noise. If an element doesn't serve a job, it's deleted in the report.
**Errors communicated well:** every error states what happened, why, and what to do — never just "Error".
**Help & documentation:** help exists where users get stuck, not in a help center nobody visits.

workflows.section: 4. THE ACCESSIBILITY PASS (Short Version — See taste-accessibility)

items.text: Tab through: focus visible at every stop; no traps; logical order.
Every input labeled; every button/link has text; alt text is meaningful or empty.
Contrast spot-check on every distinct surface (heading/body/button/placeholder).
`prefers-reduced-motion` handled; anything autoplaying or auto-advancing paused.

workflows.section: 5. THE CONVERSION PASS (If Asked to Improve, Not Just Audit)

items.text: One primary CTA above the fold; secondary actions visually quieter or deferred.
The value proposition lands in ≤ 8 seconds (headline does it, not the sub-sub-line).
Friction inventory: fields, steps, and clicks between "interested" and "started" — each one justified.
Trust signals exist where decisions happen (near CTA, in pricing): social proof, guarantees, no-fine-print.
[ ] No screenshots were taken/reviewed (never audit from code alone).
[ ] Findings lack severities or screenshot references.
[ ] Slop patterns dismissed as "style preference" (they're P1).
[ ] Anything on the page was fixed before the full audit pass completed.
[ ] The verdict doesn't name a single most-important change.
